About Carlisle Companies Incorporated

Carlisle Companies Incorporated is a leading supplier of innovative building envelope products and solutions for more energy efficient buildings. Through its building products businesses – Carlisle Construction Materials ("CCM") and Carlisle Weatherproofing Technologies ("CWT") – and family of leading brands, Carlisle delivers innovative, labor reducing and environmentally responsible products and solutions to customers through the Carlisle Experience. Carlisle is committed to generating superior shareholder returns and maintaining a balanced capital deployment approach, including investments in our businesses, strategic acquisitions, share repurchases and continued dividend increases. Leveraging its culture of continuous improvement as embodied in the Carlisle Operating System ("COS"), Carlisle has committed to achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.

MADISON, Wis., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Accuray Incorporated (NASDAQ: ARAY) today reported, as required by NASDAQ Listing Rules, equity inducement awards to Sofiane Laoussadi, the company's new Senior Vice President, Global Services & Solutions.

As a material inducement to Mr. Laoussadi joining the company, and in accordance with NASDAQ Listing Rule 5635(c)(4), the Compensation Committee approved granting to Mr. Laoussadi (i) an award of 650,000 restricted stock units covering shares of the company's common stock and (ii) an award of 650,000 performance-based restricted stock units (at target) covering shares of the company's common stock, in each case effective as of October 30, 2026 (collectively, the "Inducement Awards"). The Inducement Awards were made outside of the company's current equity plan but are subject to terms and conditions generally consistent with those in the company's 2026 Equity Incentive Plan.

One-fourth (1/4) of the underlying shares subject to the restricted stock unit award will vest on October 30, 2027, and will continue to vest as to one-fourth (1/4) of the underlying shares subject to the restricted stock unit award on each yearly anniversary of such date, subject in each case to Mr. Laoussadi's continued service through the applicable vesting date.

The performance-based restricted stock unit award have a performance period ending on the last day of the company's 2028 fiscal year and will vest based on the achievement of performance criteria and other terms as determined by the Compensation Committee for performance based restricted stock units granted to other similarly situated senior executives of the company, subject to Mr. Laoussadi's continued service and the terms of the applicable award agreement.

About Accuray
Accuray is committed to expanding the powerful potential of radiation therapy to improve as many lives as possible. We invent unique, market-changing solutions designed to deliver radiation treatments for even the most complex cases—while making commonly treatable cases even easier—to meet the full spectrum of patient needs. We are dedicated to continuous innovation in radiation therapy for oncology, neuro-radiosurgery, and beyond, as we partner with clinicians and administrators, empowering them to help patients get back to their lives, faster. Accuray is headquartered in Madison, Wisconsin, with facilities worldwide. To learn more, visit www.accuray.com or follow us on Facebook, LinkedIn, X, and YouTube.

ANDOVER, Mass., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TransMedics Group, Inc. ("TransMedics") (Nasdaq: TMDX), a medical technology company that is transforming organ transplant therapy for patients with end-stage lung, heart, and liver failure, today announced that on October 28, 2026, the Company granted non-qualified stock options to purchase an aggregate of 71,815 shares of its common stock and an aggregate of 47,924 restricted stock units (RSUs) to nine employees. These awards were granted as a material inducement for each employee's entry into employment with TransMedics.

The grants included stock options to purchase 34,419 shares of TransMedics' common stock and 22,969 RSUs granted to Fernando Araujo, the Company's Chief Financial Officer. The grants were approved by the Compensation Committee of the TransMedics Board of Directors and granted in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) and pursuant to the TransMedics Group, Inc. Inducement Plan.

The stock options were granted with a per share exercise price of $66.90, the closing price of the common stock on the Nasdaq Global Market on October 28, 2026. Twenty-five percent of the shares subject to each option grant will vest on the first anniversary of the date of the employee's start of employment, with the remainder vesting in equal monthly installments over the subsequent three-year period, subject to the employee's continued service with the Company through the applicable vesting date. The options have a 10-year term and are subject to the terms of the TransMedics Group, Inc. Inducement Plan. Twenty-five percent of each RSU award will vest on the first four anniversaries of the date of the employee's start of employment, subject to the employee's continued service with the Company through the applicable vesting date. The RSUs are subject to the terms of the TransMedics Group, Inc. Inducement Plan.

About TransMedics Group, Inc. 
TransMedics is the world's leader in portable extracorporeal warm perfusion and assessment of donor organs for transplantation. Headquartered in Andover, Massachusetts, the company was founded to address the unmet need for more and better organs for transplantation and has developed technologies to preserve organ quality, assess organ viability prior to transplant, and potentially increase the utilization of donor organs for the treatment of end-stage heart, lung, and liver failure.

MOOSIC, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Peoples Financial Services Corp. (“Peoples” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: PFIS), the bank holding company for Peoples Security Bank and Trust Company (the “Bank”), today reported unaudited financial results at and for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Peoples reported net income of $19.1 million, or $1.90 per diluted share for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $3.9 million compared to net income of $15.2 million, or $1.51 per diluted share for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $48.7 million, or $4.85 per diluted share, an increase of $1.5 million, compared to $47.2 million, or $4.69 per diluted share for the same nine months of 2025. Return on average assets (“ROAA”) and return on average equity (“ROAE”) on an annualized basis for the three months ended September 30, 2026, were 1.41% and 14.07%, respectively, compared to 1.19% and 12.02%, respectively, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, annualized ROAA and ROAE were 1.23% and 12.16%, respectively, compared to 1.25% and 12.86%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in net income for both the three- and nine-month periods was primarily attributable to higher net interest income and non-interest income, partially offset by increases in non-interest expense. For the three-month period ending September 30, 2026, there was a benefit of credit losses whereas the nine-month period recognized a provision of credit losses that partially offset the increase in net income for the year-to-date period.

“We are pleased with our strong third-quarter performance, highlighted by meaningful growth in net income and improved returns on both assets and equity. Higher net interest income and non-interest income reflect the strength of our core business, the dedication of our team, and our disciplined execution” commented Gerard A. Champi, President & CEO. “These results underscore the resilience and strength of our franchise and our continued focus on creating long-term value for our shareholders. As we move forward, we remain committed on delivering consistent financial performance while continuing to invest in our customers, employees, and the communities we serve.” concluded Mr. Champi.

In addition to evaluating its results of operations in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), Peoples routinely supplements its evaluation with an analysis of certain non-GAAP financial measures, such as tangible stockholders’ equity, core net income, and tax-equivalent net interest income and related ratios, among others. The reported results included in this release contain items, which Peoples considers non-core, namely net gains and losses on the sale of available for sale investment securities and acquisition-related expenses. Peoples believes the reported non-GAAP financial measures provide information useful to investors in understanding its operating performance and trends. Where non-GAAP disclosures are used in this press release, a reconciliation to the comparable GAAP measure is provided in the accompanying tables. The non-GAAP financial measures Peoples uses may differ from the non-GAAP financial measures of other financial institutions and should not be viewed as a substitute for GAAP.

NOTABLES

  • On a linked quarter basis, total loans increased $60.7 million, or 5.6% annualized, to $4.4 billion as of September 30, 2026, from $4.3 billion as of June 30, 2026, and increased $347.1 million, or 8.6% annualized, from $4.0 billion as of September 30, 2025.
  • Nonperforming assets were $10.3 million as of September 30, 2026, an improvement of $4.4 million from $14.7 million as of June 30, 2026, and $6.5 million from $16.8 million at September 30, 2025. Nonperforming assets represented 0.24% of loans, net and foreclosed assets as of September 30, 2026, versus 0.34% and 0.42% of loans, net and foreclosed assets as of June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.
  • On a linked quarter basis, total deposits increased $163.3 million, or 14.4% annualized, to $4.7 billion as of September 30, 2026, from $4.5 billion as of June 30, 2026, and increased $382.4 million, or 8.9%, from $4.3 billion as of September 30, 2025.
  • Book value per common share at September 30, 2026, increased $1.92 to $52.87 from $50.95 at September 30, 2025. Tangible book value per common share, a non-GAAP measure1, increased $2.52 to $42.95 at September 30, 2026, compared to $40.43 at September 30, 2025.

INCOME STATEMENT REVIEW

  • Net income increased $3.9 million, or 25.5%, to $19.1 million from $15.2 million in the year ago quarter and $4.3 million, or 29.2%, from $14.8 million for the three months ending June 30, 2026. Net income increased to $48.7 million, or 3.1%, from $47.2 million for the nine months ending September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively.
  • Net interest margin (“NIM”), calculated on a fully taxable equivalent (“FTE”) basis, a non-GAAP measure1, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, improved 26 basis points to 3.80% as compared to 3.54% for the three months ended September 30, 2025, but contracted 2 basis points from 3.82% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, the FTE NIM, a non-GAAP measure1, improved 19 basis points to 3.77% in 2026 from 3.58% in 2025.
  • The FTE yield on interest-earning assets, a non-GAAP measure1, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, increased 15 basis points to 5.71% from 5.56% from the three months ended September 30, 2025, and increased 7 basis points from 5.64% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the FTE yield on interest-earning assets, a non-GAAP measure1, was 5.62%, an increase of 4 basis points from 5.58% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • The cost of funds, which represents the average rate paid on total interest-bearing liabilities, decreased 15 basis points to 2.49% from 2.64% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025 respectively. The cost of funds increased 9 basis points from 2.40% from the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine-month periods ended September 30, the cost of funds was 2.43% in 2026, a reduction of 18 basis points compared to 2.61% for 2025.
  • The cost of interest-bearing deposits decreased 13 basis points to 2.26% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from 2.39% as of the three months ended September 30, 2025, but increased 12 basis points from 2.14% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the cost of interest-bearing deposits decreased 23 basis points to 2.19% from 2.42% for the same nine months of 2025.
  • The cost of total deposits, which includes the impact of noninterest-bearing deposits, was 1.79% for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 9 basis points from 1.88% for the third quarter of 2025. However, the cost of total deposits increased 11 basis points compared to 1.68% for the second quarter of 2026. The cost of deposits for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was 1.72%, a decrease of 20 basis points from 1.92% for the comparable period of 2025.

Third Quarter 2026 Results – Comparison to Second Quarter 2026 and Third Quarter 2025

Net interest income increased $6.1 million to $47.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $41.2 million for the prior year third quarter. FTE net interest income, a non-GAAP measure1, increased $6.4 million to $48.3 million as of September 30, 2026, from $41.9 million at September 30, 2025. Specifically, the increase in FTE net interest income, a non-GAAP measure1, resulted largely from a $6.5 million increase in FTE interest income, while interest expense increased modestly by $0.2 million. The increase in interest income reflected improved earning asset yields and an increase in loan volume, while lower deposit and borrowing costs almost entirely offset the impact of growth in interest-bearing liabilities on interest expense. Linked quarter net interest income increased $1.7 million from $45.6 million at June 30, 2026. FTE net interest income for the linked quarters increased $1.8 million from $46.5 million in June 2026, which was due to a $3.8 million increase in FTE interest income, partially offset by a $2.0 million increase in interest expense. The linked quarters saw increases in funding costs as the Company utilized CD specials, brokered deposits and FHLB advances to fund loan growth.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a benefit for credit losses of $1.1 million, compared to a benefit of $0.8 million for the same period in 2025, and a provision of $3.1 million for the second quarter of 2026. The reduction in credit provisioning reflected improved asset quality metrics, seasoning of the equipment loan segment and lower specific reserves resulting from the successful resolution of nonperforming loans.

Noninterest income was $5.7 million and $5.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The Company recorded a loss on the sales of administrative offices of $0.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. There were no such losses recorded during the third quarter of 2026. Non-interest income decreased $0.8 million from $6.5 million for the linked quarter ending June 30, 2026, primarily due to decreases in merchant services and service charges and the absence of the $0.3 million gain on the sale of a branch property that was part of a sale/leaseback transaction in the second quarter of 2026.

The current quarter’s non-interest expense increased $3.0 million to $31.7 million from the prior year’s same quarter non-interest expense of $28.7 million. Salaries and employee benefits increased $1.5 million associated with merit increases, staff additions, and higher benefit costs. Other expenses increased $1.1 million primarily due to increases in corporate business development and professional fees. Noninterest expense increased by $1.1 million from $30.6 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Salaries increased $0.5 million, which primarily reflected staff additions and higher stock-based compensation expenses. Occupancy and equipment expenses increased $0.4 million resulting from higher data processing expenses. The efficiency ratio, a non-GAAP measure1, was 56.12% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase as compared to 55.16% for the linked quarter ended June 30, 2026, but an improvement from 56.52% from the prior year quarter ended September 30, 2025.

Income tax expense was $3.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, and $3.6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The effective tax rate was 14.6% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, 19.1% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, and 19.6% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The decrease in the effective tax rate for the current quarter was largely due to the purchase of 2025 federal tax credits during the three months ended September 30, 2026, which reduced income tax expense by $1.2 million.

Nine-Month Results – Comparison to Prior Year First Nine Months

Net interest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, increased $12.9 million to $135.8 million from $122.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. On an FTE basis, net interest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, increased $13.4 million to $138.5 million from $125.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in FTE net interest income was due to an $11.6 million increase in tax-equivalent interest income, a non-GAAP measure1, coupled with a $1.8 million decrease in interest expense. The Company’s net interest spread widened 22 basis points to 3.19% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from 2.97% for the same nine-month period of 2025. Additionally, comparing the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company’s FTE net interest margin improved by 19 basis points to 3.77% from 3.58%, respectively.

The increase in fully tax-equivalent interest income was driven primarily by higher earning asset balances, particularly taxable loans, and by higher balances and yields on tax-exempt investment securities. Lower overall FTE yields, mainly on taxable investments, partially offset these benefits.

Total average earning assets increased $241.4 million to $4.9 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $4.7 billion for the same nine months of 2025. Average taxable loans increased $245.4 million to $4.0 billion from $3.7 billion comparing the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The yield on taxable loans decreased 10 basis points to 6.03% from 6.13% between the two periods, which primarily reflected a 75 basis point reduction in the prime rate during the second half of 2025 offset slightly by the increase of 25 basis points in September 2026. Accretion associated with purchase accounting fair value discounts on purchased loans was $9.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12.2 million for the same period of 2025. Average tax-exempt investments totaled $157.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $66.7 million from $90.9 million for the same nine-month period ended September 30, 2025, while taxable investments averaged $430.9 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $549.8 million at September 30, 2025. Average interest earning deposits increased by $58.1 million to $100.9 million at September 30, 2026, from $42.8 million at September 30, 2025. The FTE yield on investments increased 76 basis points to 3.87% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from 3.11% for the same nine months of 2025.

Interest expense decreased $1.8 million to $68.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $70.0 million for the same period in 2025, primarily due to lower average deposit rates overall, coupled with a reduction in average small dollar time deposits, which offset net balance increases in the non-maturing deposit portfolio. These benefits were partially offset by higher average balances on borrowings and subordinated debt exceeding reductions in borrowing rates. The average rate paid on interest-bearing deposits decreased 23 basis points to 2.19% from 2.42%, reflecting lower market rates in 2026 in addition to lower costs related to interest bearing demand accounts when compared to 2025.

Average small dollar time deposits, which include brokered deposits, decreased $68.5 million to $321.3 million, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $389.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The average rate paid for small dollar time deposits decreased 53 basis points to 3.29% from 3.82% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively, partially the result of a reduction of $50.9 million in average brokered deposits, which the Company let roll off at maturity. These higher-costing deposits were replaced with lower cost non-maturing deposits and borrowings. Average subordinated debt increased $25.9 million to $83.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $57.4 million for the same period in 2025, while the average rate paid on subordinated debt increased 93 basis points to 8.42% from 7.49% for the periods ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively, due to a net new issuance of subordinated debt in the second quarter of 2025 in the amount of $52 million.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the provision for credit losses was $3.3 million, an increase of $4.2 million from a $0.9 million benefit recorded for the same nine months of 2025. The increase in loan provisioning in the first nine months of 2026 was primarily impacted by significant loan growth, while the benefit in the first nine months of the prior year reflected reductions in non-accrual assets and declines in model loss rates.

Noninterest income was $19.1 million and $18.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The $1.1 million increase in noninterest income was primarily due to increases in interest rate swap income of $0.6 million, along with combined net gains of $0.5 million on the sale of investment securities available for sale, a $0.3 million gain on the sale and market value appreciation of equity securities and a $0.4 million increase in mortgage banking income, partially offset by a decrease in service charge, fee, and commission income of $0.7 million. The current nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, includes a gain on the sale of a branch property of $0.3 million that was part of the aforementioned sale/leaseback transaction. The comparable prior year period included a loss of $0.6 million on the sales of administrative offices, offset by gain of $0.7 million on the sale of the Company’s former corporate headquarters in Scranton, PA.

Noninterest expense increased $7.9 million to $92.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $84.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase is primarily due to increases in salaries and employee benefits expenses, occupancy and equipment expenses, and other expenses. Salaries and employee benefits expense was $45.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $41.4 million for the same nine months in 2025. The $3.8 million increase resulted primarily from annual merit increases, staff additions and higher health insurance costs. Net occupancy and equipment expenses were $22.7 million for the first nine months of 2026, an increase of $2.6 million from $20.1 million for the same nine-month period in 2025. The increase was largely caused by higher rent expenses associated with the new corporate headquarters and increases in data processing expenses related to the implementation of an on-line account opening platform. Other expenses increased $2.6 million to $17.7 million from $15.1 million for the nine months ending September 30, 2025. This increase in other expenses includes an increase in advertising, corporate business development, and legal expenses. The efficiency ratio, a non-GAAP measure1, was 56.10% in 2026 and 55.38% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively.

Income tax expense was $10.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $10.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate was 18.0% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 17.9% in the prior year’s same nine-month period.

BALANCE SHEET REVIEW

Total loans were $4.4 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $60.7 million compared to $4.3 billion at June 30, 2026, and an increase of $347.1 million compared to $4.0 billion at September 30, 2025. Comparing September 30, 2026, and 2025, the Company saw strong demand in all markets for commercial and residential real estate loans, commercial and industrial loans, and municipal loans, with decreases seen in the Company’s equipment financing and indirect auto loan portfolio. Comparing September 30, 2026, to June 30, 2026, increases were observed in the commercial and industrial portfolio and in the commercial and residential real estate portfolio. Consumer loans and the equipment financing portfolios were relatively flat, while the indirect auto portfolio decreased.

Total investments were $510.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $529.6 million at June 30, 2026, and $610.3 million at September 30, 2025. At September 30, 2026, available for sale securities totaled $440.8 million, a decrease of $17.3 million from $458.1 million at June 30, 2026, and a decrease of $93.7 million from $534.5 million at September 30, 2025. Held to maturity securities totaled $66.7 million at September 30, 2026, a decrease of $2.1 million from $68.8 million at June 30, 2026, and a decrease of $6.6 million from $73.3 million at September 30, 2025. Due to strong loan demand, cash flows from repayments of investment securities and a portion of the proceeds from sales of investments during the first three months of 2026 were redirected and used to fund loan growth.

Total deposits were $4.7 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $163.3 million from $4.5 billion at June 30, 2026, and an increase of $382.4 million from $4.3 billion at September 30, 2025. Noninterest-bearing deposits increased $24.5 million to $971.0 million at September 30, 2026, from $946.5 million at June 30, 2026, and increased $59.1 million from $912.0 million at September 30, 2025. Interest-bearing deposits increased $138.7 million to $3.7 billion from $3.6 billion at June 30, 2026, and increased $323.4 million from $3.4 billion at September 30, 2025, primarily reflecting a strategic deposit growth effort which offset a decrease in brokered deposits. Brokered deposits represented 5.4% of total deposits at September 30, 2026, and 7.7% of total deposits at June 30, 2026, compared with 3.9% at September 30, 2025. Approximately 34.8% of deposits were uninsured at September 30, 2026, compared with 31.0% uninsured at June 30, 2026, and 32.3% at September 30, 2025.

The Company maintained a strong capital position at September 30, 2026. Stockholders’ equity equaled $529.3 million or $52.87 per share at September 30, 2026, compared to $536.2 million or $53.56 per share at June 30, 2026, and $509.3 million, or $50.95 per share at September 30, 2025. Stockholders’ equity was impacted by net income, offset by dividends to shareholders and an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss primarily due to market rate adjustments related to available for sale investments.

Tangible book value, a non-GAAP measure1 was $42.95 per share at September 30, 2026, $43.51 per share at June 30, 2026, and $40.43 at September 30, 2025. The Company declared quarterly dividends of $0.625 for each quarter of 2026 and $0.6175 for the quarter ending September 30, 2025. Dividends for the year totaled $1.875 per share for 2026 and $1.853 per share for 2025.

ASSET QUALITY REVIEW

The Company experienced strong improvement in asset quality during the three- and nine-month periods of 2026. Nonperforming assets, which include nonperforming loans, loans past due 90 days or more and still accruing, and foreclosed assets, were $10.3 million or 0.24% of loans, net and foreclosed assets, at September 30, 2026, a $4.4 million decrease compared to $14.7 million, or 0.34% of loans, net and foreclosed assets at June 30, 2026. The linked-quarter decrease was primarily due to favorable resolutions of several nonaccrual assets during the third quarter of 2026. Key Terms

roaafinancial
Return on Average Assets (ROAA) measures how efficiently a company turns its assets into profit by dividing net profit over a period by the average total assets it held during that period. It matters to investors because it shows whether a business is getting a good return from what it owns—like judging a car’s fuel efficiency by miles per gallon—helping compare profitability across companies of different sizes.
roaefinancial
ROAE stands for Return on Average Equity, a profitability ratio that shows how much net income a company generates for its owners relative to the average amount of shareholder equity invested over a period. It’s like measuring the interest rate a business pays its owners on the capital they’ve left in the company, with the ‘average’ smoothing out swings in equity during the year. Investors use ROAE to compare how efficiently different companies turn owner capital into profits and to assess management’s ability to deliver returns over time.
gaapfinancial
GAAP, or Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, are a set of standardized rules and guidelines that companies follow when preparing their financial statements. They ensure consistency, transparency, and comparability across different companies, making it easier for investors to understand and compare financial information accurately. This helps investors make informed decisions based on trustworthy and uniform financial reports.
View in glossary
non-gaapfinancial
Non-GAAP refers to financial measures that companies use to show their earnings or performance without including certain expenses or income that are often added back to give a different picture. It matters because it can make a company's results look better or more favorable, but it may also hide important costs, so investors need to look at both GAAP (official rules) and non-GAAP numbers to get a full understanding.
View in glossary
net interest marginfinancial
Net interest margin measures how much a bank earns from lending and investing compared with what it pays for funding, expressed as a percentage of its interest-earning assets. Think of it like a grocery store’s markup: it shows the gap between buying cost and selling price per dollar of goods — here, the cost is interest paid and the sale is interest received. Investors watch it because a higher margin usually means a bank is more profitable and better at managing interest rate and credit conditions.
fully taxable equivalentfinancial
A fully taxable equivalent converts a tax-free yield into the pretax yield you would need from a taxable investment to get the same after-tax return, using an investor’s marginal tax rate. Think of it like inflating a discounted price to the full sticker price so you can compare items side‑by‑side; investors use it to fairly compare tax-exempt securities with taxable alternatives and choose the better after-tax income.

VANCOUVER, BC and BOSTON, MA, Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Xenon Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: XENE), a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to drug discovery, clinical development, and commercialization of life-changing therapeutics for patients in need, today announced equity inducement grants to nine new non-officer employees consisting of an aggregate of 24,250 share options and 14,250 restricted share units (RSUs). All of the foregoing share options and RSUs were approved by the Compensation Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors with an effective date of October 29, 2026 and were granted as inducements material to the employees entering into employment with the Company in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

The share options have an exercise price of $37.54 per common share, which is equal to the closing price per share of Xenon’s common shares on the grant date of October 29, 2026. The share option grants vest over four years, with 25% vesting on the one-year anniversary of the respective employee’s start date and 1/36th of the remaining options vesting monthly thereafter on the last day of each month, subject to such option recipient’s continued service relationship with the Company. Each option has a 10-year term and is subject to the terms and conditions of the share option agreement and the terms of the Company’s Amended and Restated 2025 Inducement Equity Incentive Plan. The RSUs will vest as to 25% of the underlying shares on each of the first four anniversaries of the grant date of October 29, 2026, subject to such employee’s continued service relationship with the Company. Loan balances are generally flat nine months to date, but we actually booked $363 million over the period in lines of credit and term loans. Balances have been impacted partly by strategic paydowns in leasing and SBA, which totaled $43 million for the nine months, as well as competition from PE firms.

The wealth group grew quarterly pre-tax income by 35% over the third quarter of 2025 due to higher AUM, better efficiencies, and a good referral pipeline from our commercial group. Our mortgage group had a down third quarter, which is historically the most productive, as closed loans declined 27% from the prior quarter. Low housing inventory is dogging the industry with higher rates having a lesser impact. Mortgage’s quarterly pre-tax loss of $1.6 million included a non-operating $955 thousand loss on a small portfolio of mortgage loans that are fair-valued quarterly. We continue to make mortgage cost adjustments to align with volume.

We remain intensely focused on resolving non-performing loans without incurring elevated charge-offs. We had improvements in the third quarter, but this takes time and should result in stronger recoveries. We have strengthened our treasury and payments teams with experienced industry professionals in a concentrated effort to improve our deposit franchise and expect this to yield good results in 2027. Asset Quality Summary

Non-performing loans decreased $3.8 million, or 4.6%, to $78.3 million as of September 30, 2026 compared to $82.1 million at June 30, 2026, with the major drivers of this decline from land development loans ($1.8 million), SBA loans ($1.0 million), and commercial mortgage loans ($807 thousand). The decrease in land development loans was the result of a $1.8 million loan being reclassified to loans held for sale as of September 30, 2026 due to pending note sale, while the decrease in commercial mortgage non-performing loans was the result of the reclassification of a loan relationship out of non-performing as these loans were in the process of collection as of September 30, 2026. The decline in non-performing SBA loans was partly due to an increase in charge-offs during the third quarter, combined with a lower level of SBA loans added to non-performing loan category in the third quarter, compared to the second quarter. SBA loans make up $23.6 million of total non-performing loans, with $13.6 million, or 57.6%, guaranteed by the SBA. The SBA portfolio was subject to the Fed's rapid rate increase with 48.1%, of total non-performing SBA loans having been originated in 2020-2021 when rates were over 500 basis points lower.

The ratio of non-performing loans to total loans as of September 30, 2026 was 3.55%, down from 3.68% as of June 30, 2026, due to the decrease in non-performing loans detailed above. The ratio of non-performing loans to total loans, excluding the guaranteed portion of the SBA portfolio (a non-GAAP measure) was 2.93% as of September 30, 2026. As of September 30, 2026 there were specific reserves of $3.0 million against individually evaluated loans, a decrease of $237 thousand from June 30, 2026. Non-performing loans decreased $3.8 million from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026 and another $2.7 million settled subsequent to September 30, 2026, a combined reduction of $6.5 million or 8%.

Net charge-offs decreased to $1.9 million, or 0.09% of total average loans for the third quarter, compared to net charge-offs of $2.6 million, or 0.12%, for the second quarter. Third quarter charge-offs were driven by $934 thousand in SBA loans, $1.2 million in finance receivables, $413 thousand of small ticket equipment leases, and $125 thousand in commercial loans. Partially offsetting third quarter charge-offs were recoveries of $739 thousand mainly between SBA loans, finance receivables, and leases.

The ratio of allowance for credit losses to total loans held for investment was 0.96% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 0.99% reported as of June 30, 2026. The decline in this coverage ratio was due to a large percentage of charge-offs for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 being against loans that were specifically reserved for in prior quarters.

data.description:
Higher quarterly earnings accompanied lower deposits, reduced available liquidity and an equity decline driven primarily by unrealized losses.

WARRENTON, VA / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Oak View Bankshares, Inc. (the "Company") (OTCID:OAKV), parent company of Oak View National Bank (the "Bank"), reported net income of $2.85 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $1.89 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $6.50 million, compared to $5.27 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Basic and diluted earnings per share were $0.82 per share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $0.54 per share for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Basic and diluted earnings per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, were $1.86 per share compared to $1.59 per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Michael Ewing, CEO and Chairman of the Board, said, "Our third quarter results reflect the continued strength of our community banking franchise and the successful execution of our long-term strategic objectives. During the quarter, our tireless team continued to earn lending and deposit market share. We maintained exceptional asset quality with no nonperforming loans, no nonaccrual loans, no loans past due 90 days or more and no loan charge-offs. Finally, we took advantage of market opportunities to execute several balance sheet management initiatives, which further balanced our interest rate risk profile, while maintaining robust on- and off-balance sheet liquidity." Mr. Ewing continued, "Our team is focused and energized, knowing that our balance sheet is well-positioned to thrive across multiple rate scenarios and over time. As always, everything we do aims to deliver long-term value to our shareholders, customers, and communities."

Selected Highlights:

  • The return on average assets and return on average equity for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, reflect strong earnings performance and disciplined balance sheet management. Return on average assets was 1.17% and return on average equity was 19.89% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 0.93% and 15.90%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Return on average assets was 0.92% and return on average equity was 15.24% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 0.93% and 15.99%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Several balance sheet management initiatives were executed during the quarter, including the sale of $50.00 million of U.S. Treasury securities, the repayment of $30.00 million in short-term borrowings, and the termination of $90.50 million (notional value) of hedged positions. These actions, in part, generated a non-recurring benefit of approximately $367,000 to net interest income while, on a go-forward basis, are expected to improve liquidity, further optimize the interest rate risk profile and potentially enhance net interest income from the relief of short-term borrowings.
  • Total assets were $934.10 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $878.24 million on December 31, 2025, an increase of $55.86 million.
  • Total loans were $399.24 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $349.89 million on December 31, 2025, an increase of $49.35 million.
  • The total carrying value of debt securities was $456.63 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $463.02 million on December 31, 2025, a decrease of $6.39 million.
  • Total deposits were $705.77 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $713.58 million on December 31, 2025, a decrease of $7.81 million, which reflected an increase in core deposits of $48.38 million and a decrease in brokered deposits of $56.19 million.
  • Asset quality continues to be outstanding. No loans were charged off during the quarter, and as of September 30, 2026, there were no nonperforming loans, nonaccrual loans, or loans past due 90 days or more.
  • Liquidity remains strong, with cash, unencumbered securities available for sale, and available secured and unsecured borrowing capacity totaling $419.40 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $574.44 million as of December 31, 2025.
  • Capital levels remained a key strength as of September 30, 2026. The Bank exceeded all regulatory "well-capitalized" standards, reporting a total capital ratio of 17.08%, Tier 1 capital and Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratios of 16.31%, and a leverage ratio of 8.54% at quarter-end.

Net Interest Income
The net interest margin was 3.13% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 2.98% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Net interest income before the provision for credit losses was $6.81 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.52 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Average earning assets and the related yield were $930.66 million and 5.75%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $760.69 million and 5.84%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Average interest-bearing liabilities and the related cost of funds, which include average noninterest-bearing deposits, were $904.24 million and 2.69%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $757.05 million and 2.87%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

The net interest margin was 2.87% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 2.96% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Net interest income before the provision for credit losses was $18.09 million and $15.77 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Average earning assets and the related yield were $906.11 million and 5.63%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $720.30 million and 5.73%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Average interest-bearing liabilities and the related cost of funds, which include average noninterest-bearing deposits, were $883.36 million and 2.83%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $707.34 million and 2.82%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Noninterest Income
Noninterest income was $538,000 and $1.61 million for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $427,000 and $1.54 million for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Significant changes in noninterest income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same periods in 2025, were:

  • Interchange fee income was $283,000 and $254,000 for the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Interchange fee income was $827,000 and $677,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. These fluctuations were primarily related to transaction volume.
  • Mortgage loan fee income was $114,000 and $22,000 for the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Mortgage loan fee income was $181,000 and $332,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The quarterly fluctuations were primarily due to transaction volume while the fluctuations for the nine-month periods were the result of the current interest rate environment compared to the same periods of 2025.

Noninterest Expense
Noninterest expenses were $4.03 million and $3.61 million for the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Noninterest expenses were $12.02 million and $10.52 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The net noninterest margin, which is defined as noninterest expense less noninterest income to average assets, was 1.43% and 1.56% for the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively, and 1.47% and 1.59% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. While noninterest expenses have increased 11.81% and 14.23% for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same periods of 2025, the most significant increases were attributable to regulatory assessments and other taxes associated with the Company's continued growth. While total noninterest expenses increased for the periods noted, the net noninterest margin indicates overhead is being consistently managed and controlled.

Asset Quality
With no nonperforming loans, nonaccrual loans or loans 90 days or more past due on September 30, 2026, these asset quality metrics continued to reflect the Bank's conservative underwriting practices and disciplined credit administration.

The allowance for credit losses related to the loan portfolio was $3.68 million and $3.22 million as of September 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, respectively, or 0.92% of total loans outstanding, net of unearned income, for both periods presented.

The provision for credit losses was $75,000 for each of the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, and $466,000 and $236,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The provision for credit losses for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily driven by strong loan growth during the period and the resulting increase in required reserves under the Company's CECL methodology.

Shareholders' Equity & Regulatory Capital
Shareholders' equity was $48.17 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $57.74 million on December 31, 2025. Despite the decline in shareholders' equity resulting primarily from unrealized losses recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income, the Bank remained well capitalized under all applicable regulatory standards, with capital ratios substantially exceeding regulatory minimums and well-capitalized thresholds.

Accumulated other comprehensive loss was $11.94 million on September 30, 2026, or 2.72% of the total securities available-for-sale portfolio. These market-driven unrealized losses within the municipal securities portfolio are partially offset by unrealized gains on hedged positions and reflect changes in market interest rates rather than deterioration in the underlying credit quality or expected cash flows of the securities portfolio. Management has prudently managed the Company's interest rate risk position and believes these fluctuations are largely attributable to changes in market conditions and interest rates.

About Oak View Bankshares, Inc. and Oak View National Bank
The Company's common stock is listed for trading on the OTC Market Group's OTCID-Basic Market, http://www.otcmarkets.com, under the ticker symbol OAKV.

The Company's common stock closed at a price of $19.45 per share on October 29, 2026.

The Company's book value per share was $13.81 as of September 30, 2026.

Oak View Bankshares, Inc. is the parent bank holding company for Oak View National Bank, a locally owned and managed community bank serving Fauquier, Culpeper, Rappahannock, and surrounding counties. For more information about Oak View Bankshares, Inc. and Oak View National Bank, please visit our website at www.oakviewbank.com. Member FDIC.

All-New Polaris-Engineered RZR Pro R Factory Boost Delivers 400 Horsepower and Purpose-Built Enhancements for Open Desert Racing, Joining the RZR Pro R Factory in Polaris' Race Machine Lineup Available for Purchase

MINNEAPOLIS, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Polaris and RZR Factory Racing today unveiled the all-new RZR Pro R Factory Boost at the company's annual Camp RZR event at Glamis Imperial Sand Dunes. Delivering up to 400 horsepower, the RZR Pro R Factory Boost is designed and developed by Polaris engineers and built in Roseau, Minnesota, bringing a bigger, stronger and even more capable package to the race-proven platform.

Joining rather than replacing the existing Gen 2 RZR Pro R Factory, the new model gives racers another purpose-built option with a different level of performance and capability. Together, the two platforms strengthen Polaris' race vehicle lineup and its commitment to delivering race-ready side-by-sides designed to rule every race.

The RZR Pro R Factory Boost builds on the foundation established by the recently introduced production RZR Pro R Boost while incorporating proven components and lessons learned from the Gen 2 RZR Pro R Factory. Engineered specifically for competition, the new race machine further refines power delivery, chassis design, cooling and suspension to meet the demands of high-speed desert racing.

"The Gen 2 RZR Pro R Factory has proven itself as the benchmark in the side-by-side category and demonstrated our ability to compete among the best, beating all other UTVs in virtually every major offroad race in the world. With the RZR Pro R Factory Boost, we're building on that success with a clear goal: to keep pushing the boundaries of performance and give our team and customers every advantage to continue winning at the highest level," said Alex Scheuerell, Polaris' Director of Off-Road Motorsports. "Desert racing demands strength, speed and durability across hundreds of miles, and we've engineered this platform to take on the next level of competition. We're ready to put it to the test and push for results that reflect the ambition of our team."

The RZR Pro R Factory Boost includes the following race modifications:

  • Turbocharged Power – A race-tuned, turbocharged ProStar Fury 2.0L four-cylinder engine delivers up to 400 horsepower for commanding holeshots, high-speed passes, and the power to attack demanding terrain.
  • Performance Race-Spec Chassis – The reinforced chassis features a wheelbase extended by 6.5 inches to a total of 111 inches, for greater straight-line stability and control over rough terrain. Increased tubing size across key structural members adds strength and stiffness to support higher speeds and the demands of desert racing.
  • Competition-Ready Cockpit and Cage – Redesigned with driver feedback in mind, the all-new cage design delivers added strength, while a cab that's two inches wider provides more cockpit space for improved comfort and legroom. The expanded design transforms the feel from a traditional side-by-side to a purpose-built race car.
  • Full Carbon Fiber Bodywork with Aerodynamic Design – Sculpted carbon fiber bodywork and an arched roofline reduce weight and improve aerodynamic efficiency at high speeds. Polaris engineers used computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model airflow at speeds exceeding 100 mph, informing the cage shape and redesigned rear body profile to optimize airflow and support high-speed desert racing performance.
  • Upgraded Fuel System – A 45-gallon (170-liter) fuel cell increases capacity over the previous-generation RZR Pro R Factory's 34-gallon system, extending its range beyond 200 miles to reduce pit stops.
  • MoTeC Components – The fully integrated MoTeC electronics package features an upgraded M150 ECU and dual power distribution modules, adding a second PDM over the Gen 2 RZR Pro R Factory for expanded power distribution and control capabilities.
  • Race-Tuned DYNAMIX DV Suspension – Three-inch internal bypass DYNAMIX DV Live Valve shocks feature race-specific components and upgraded one-inch shock shafts for increased strength and a broader dynamic range. Race-specific tuning maintains control across changing terrain, while a standard FOX steering damper absorbs large impacts to improve steering control and driver confidence at high speeds.

The RZR Pro R Factory Boost is available to order now in limited quantities through SCI Distribution, LLC, an exclusive distributor, with the first order window closing February 15, 2027. Starting at $200,000 US MSRP, the new race machine will be offered alongside the continued availability of the championship-proven RZR Pro R Factory, giving racers two platforms to choose from based on their performance needs and racing goals. Polaris will produce the RZR Pro R Factory Boost with SCI managing the sales and post-sale customer support process.

For the complete list of race-focused upgrades and technical specifications, or to submit an inquiry for purchase, visit https://www.polaris.com/en-us/off-road/rzr/models/rzr-pro-r-factory-boost/ 

The RZR Factory Racing team will debut the new RZR Pro R Factory Boost race machine at the 2027 King of The Hammers event, competing in multiple races.

To learn more about Polaris and the production RZR Pro R Boost, please visit Polaris.com/RZR or join the conversation and follow on Facebook sm, Instagram sm, YouTube sm and Xsm.

As the global leader in powersports, Polaris Inc. (NYSE: PII) has been defining and redefining outdoor adventure since 1954. Polaris delivers industry-shaping off-road vehicles, snowmobiles, boats, military, quadricycles, and commercial transportation vehicles, along with an expansive portfolio of parts, garments, and accessories. Its lineup includes some of the most iconic brands in powersports including the RANGER, RZR, Polaris XPEDITION, Bennington pontoons, Slingshot, and more. NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Please replace the release dated October 29, 2026 with the following corrected version to add the Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements paragraph at the end of the release.

Step-by-step process of how to redeem American Express Reward Dollars for a deposit into a High Yield Savings Account (HYSA) in the Amex Mobile App

The updated release reads:

American Express Connects Cash Back to High Yield Savings Accounts and Business Checking Accounts

  • U.S. Consumer Cash Back1 Card Members can now redeem Reward Dollars for a deposit into an American Express® High Yield Savings Account, and watch their savings grow with a competitive Annual Percentage Yield.
  • U.S. Business Cash Back Card Members can also now redeem Reward Dollars for a deposit into an American Express® Business Checking account.

Today, American Express introduced a new way for eligible U.S. Consumer and Business Cash Back Card Members to redeem rewards for a deposit into eligible American Express bank accounts, creating a more integrated experience across their Card and banking products and giving customers more options in how to redeem the rewards they earn.

U.S. Consumer Cash Back Card Members can now redeem Reward Dollars for a deposit directly into an American Express® High Yield Savings Account (HYSA), helping turn rewards into compounded growth2. Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card Members can also now redeem Reward Dollars for a deposit into an American Express Business Checking account.

“Card Members want their rewards to be useful, flexible, and easy to put toward the things that matter most to them,” said Corey Timlin, Senior Vice President of Consumer Banking at American Express. “With the majority of our deposits coming from existing Card Members, we have a unique opportunity to bring Cards and banking closer together. By making it possible for Card Members to turn the rewards they earn into savings and everyday banking, we’re creating a more connected experience that helps them get even more value from their relationship with American Express.”

A More Connected Membership Experience for Cash Back Card Members

  • For U.S. Consumer Cash Back Card Members, Reward Dollars can now be redeemed for a deposit directly into an Amex HYSA at a 1:1 redemption rate. Once deposited, those funds can earn the account’s competitive APY with daily compounding interest which is deposited monthly.
  • For example, Blue Cash Preferred® Card Members can earn an industry-leading 6% cash back at U.S. supermarkets on up to $6,000 in purchases per year and on select U.S. streaming subscriptions then redeem those Reward Dollars for deposits directly into an Amex HYSA with a competitive APY.
  • For Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card Members, Reward Dollars can now be redeemed for a deposit directly into an Amex Business Checking Account at a 1:1 redemption rate.
  • In 2027, American Express plans to introduce an additional feature that will give Consumer Card Members who also have an American Express HYSA the ability to automatically redeem Reward Dollars for deposits into their account.

How to Redeem Cash Back Reward Dollars for Deposits into an Amex High Yield Savings Account or a Business Checking Account

Redeeming Reward Dollars for a deposit into an Amex High Yield Savings Account or Amex Business Checking account takes just a few simple steps through an American Express online account, with redemption through the Amex App coming soon. Here’s how:

  • Log in to your American Express account online.
  • Select your eligible Cash Back Card and navigate to your Reward Dollars.
  • Choose the option to redeem Reward Dollars for a deposit into your American Express HYSA (for U.S. Consumer Cash Back Card Members) or Business Checking Account (for U.S. Business Cash Back Card Members).
  • Enter the amount of Reward Dollars you'd like to redeem for a deposit. There is no minimum redemption amount.
  • Review and confirm your redemption of Reward Dollars for a deposit directly into your HYSA or Business Checking Account (as applicable), where you can begin earning interest.

Both U.S. Consumer Cash Back and Business Card Members can also continue to redeem Reward Dollars for statement credits and toward eligible purchases at Amazon.com checkout.
